requirement:
`habeas mdbook` automatically generates one documented-coverage-gaps
subchapter under the requirements index of {cite}`requirements.index.chapter`,
whether that index is explicitly placed or automatically generated.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.test-coverage.index` has one operative clause: "`habeas mdbook` automatically generates one documented-coverage-gaps subchapter under the requirements index of {cite}`requirements.index.chapter`, whether that index is explicitly placed or automatically generated." Every part of it describes observable output. The output is one subchapter, it sits under the requirements index, and it appears whether the index is placed explicitly or generated by default.

The text names no required library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or named interface to delegate to. A different implementation would give the same book output and still satisfy the text. For example, it could build the subchapter in a different pass, or share the code path for the placed index and the default index. A clause like "one subchapter" or "under the index" says what the book looks like, not how the code is built. `requirements.index.chapter` is only cited for context. Its directive-replacement and default-chapter rules belong to that requirement, not this one.

The only supplied root is `md/reference.md#section[How%20it%20works]/section[Test%20execution%20coverage]/paragraph@c6506c25c606`. It is a documentation paragraph that holds the `{impl}` markers for `requirements.test-coverage.run` and `requirements.test-coverage.index`. It is not code, and it creates no structural obligation to check. The requirement also has test edges, which cover its behavioral obligations. Test adequacy is outside this assessment. No structural obligation needs implementation evidence, so there is no gap.

behavioral: The subject requires `habeas mdbook` to generate exactly one documented-coverage-gaps subchapter under the requirements index. That holds both when the index is explicitly placed and when it is auto-generated. I judged this from the three supplied tests. I did not read implementation source.

- **Explicit index.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` places a `{requirements-index}` directive. It filters the index's `sub_items` for chapters named "Documented coverage gaps" and asserts exactly one. It also asserts that chapter's path (`appendix/requirements-index/coverage.md`) and its `parent_names` (`["Requirements index"]`). Finally, it asserts that the index content links to it. The test also asserts `index.sub_items.len() == 6`, so there are five detail pages plus the single coverage chapter.
- **Auto-generated index.** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` has no directive. It asserts that the default index is a top-level chapter. It then asserts exactly one "Documented coverage gaps" subchapter under that index, with the expected path, parent names and link. It also asserts that the remaining sub_items are the detail pages, so the coverage chapter is not duplicated.
- **Placement under a nested index.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` covers an index that sits inside a hierarchy. It runs with numbered and unnumbered parents. It asserts that the coverage chapter is a sub-item of the index, that `parent_names` and the section number are inherited, and that the parent has two sub_items.

These tests cover both index modes, assert the "one" cardinality, and assert placement under the index. No behavioral obligation is left untested, and all three tests carry `{test}` markers for the subject.

text: subchapter under the requirements index of {cite}`requirements.index.chapter`,
whether that index is explicitly placed or automatically generated.

An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
